touches.text: Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code. That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is a script that calls the long form (eg `cairn superclaude` -> `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` -> `cairn recovery show temp`), which also saves the walk from searching farther, or does work itself (eg install). Shortcuts live beside what they serve (RULE 1). `cairn foo` whose first word is not a device means `cairn cairn foo`: top-level shortcuts are the cairn device's bin/.

Repo-root bin/ holds only the launcher itself, the one thing on PATH. Every shortcut lives in the bin/ of the device or machine it belongs to; its bin/ plus its bus verbs is what help lists at that level.
Nothing in a device's code differs by instance.
